cards.explanation: The answer is that he stations troops in every fortified city. Jehoshaphat stationed troops in every fortified city of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:2). Every fortified city, friends, not just a few of them. That's a king who means business.

The answer is True! Jehoshaphat put garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured (2 Chronicles 17:2). Asa captured them and Jehoshaphat guards them. Now THAT'S a family business.

The answer is that he walked in the earlier ways of King David. The text says the LORD was with Jehoshaphat “…because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David.” (2 Chronicles 17:3). Notice the word earlier, friends. The text says David's earlier ways. Plain and simple, and no troop count needed.

The answer is False. Jehoshaphat did not seek the Baals, the false gods (2 Chronicles 17:3). He sought the God of his father instead (2 Chronicles 17:4). No secret side-deal, bakers, and no sneaking off when nobody's looking.

The answer is Israel. The text says he “…walked by His commandments rather than the practices of Israel.” (2 Chronicles 17:4). Israel is the same Israel he was strengthening himself against back in verse 1, and he doesn't copy their practices either. He follows God's commandments, not the neighbors.

The answer is True! The LORD established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought him tribute (2 Chronicles 17:5). That means the whole of Judah, friends, not just the folks nearby. Imagine your whole neighborhood showing up at your door with gifts.

The answer is the high places and Asherah poles. The text says he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah (2 Chronicles 17:6). Right before that, the verse says his heart took delight in the ways of the LORD. Those two things sit side by side in the same verse, bakers.

The answer is teach. Jehoshaphat sent them to teach in the cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 17:7). With a king who has all those troops, you'd expect a march, but this team went out to teach. Five officials, nine Levites and two priests, and not one of them was sent to fight. That's a whole lot of teachers.

The answer is the Book of the Law of the LORD. The text says they went through the towns of Judah “…taking with them the Book of the Law of the LORD.” (2 Chronicles 17:9). The Book went with them, friends. And they taught the people in every one of those towns.

The answer is False. The dread of the LORD fell on the kingdoms around Judah, “…so that they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.” (2 Chronicles 17:10). Not one of them marched in. All those troops, bakers, and the verse puts the quiet down to the dread of the LORD.

The answer is rams and goats from their flocks. The Arabs brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 goats from their flocks (2 Chronicles 17:11). That's 7,700 of each, friends. If somebody handed me that many of anything, I'd need a bigger kitchen.

The answer is fortresses. The text says Jehoshaphat grew stronger and stronger, and he built fortresses and store cities in Judah (2 Chronicles 17:12). Stronger and stronger, and the building shows it. Then verse 13 says he kept vast supplies in the cities of Judah.
